annotate_text_path — ANNOTATE paper op

• Data kinds: image2d × text → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.annotate_text_path(img, text, path, font_size=13, color='neutral', spacing=1.0, start=0.0, draw_path=False, width=1.0, scheme='okabe_ito', font_path=None, layout=None, anchor='start', offset=0.0, upright=False, line_spacing=1.15, bold=False, italic=False) (to call the implementation directly, import annotate; annotate.annotate_text_path(img, text, path, font_size=13, color='neutral', spacing=1.0, start=0.0, draw_path=False, width=1.0, scheme='okabe_ito', font_path=None, layout=None, anchor='start', offset=0.0, upright=False, line_spacing=1.15, bold=False, italic=False); from the registry, opsannotate.get("annotate_text_path"))

Usage

Returns an image (image2d): text set along a polyline (each glyph rotated to the tangent angle).

No text backing box is laid down (it is meant to sit on top of the path). Placement, and the meaning of anchor / offset / upright (vertical writing) / line breaks via \n, are described in annotate_text_path_layout.

If layout is passed, it is used as is -- anchor and the like are ignored, so do not pass both.

bold / italic are synthesised (_bold_px / _italic_tile). Glyphs are rendered 1 at a time and then rotated, so the slant applies relative to the glyph's vertical axis (even if the path is diagonal, the italic is not skewed along the path direction).

Raises

ValueError

Same as annotate_text_path_layout + a rotated glyph goes outside the image.
